books.section: Topic 3.10 Shaping the New Republic, F. Policy Debates in the New Nation

primary_sources: Famous Whiskey Insurrection in Pennsylvania (19th-century engraving, Devens)

source: original; stimulus viewed before writing — Famous Whiskey Insurrection in Pennsylvania, 19th-century engraving (Devens). Public domain.

stimulus.text: The engraving, titled “Famous Whiskey Insurrection in Pennsylvania,” shows a large crowd in a street carrying a tarred-and-feathered effigy on poles. Banners in the crowd read “NO TAX” and “DOWN WITH TAX,” and a sign at the left reads “LIQUOR STORE.” The image is a 19th-century engraving, a later depiction of the events of 1794.
stimulus.source: Famous Whiskey Insurrection in Pennsylvania, 19th-century engraving (Devens). Public domain.
stimulus.source_note: Famous Whiskey Insurrection in Pennsylvania, 19th-century engraving (Devens). Public domain.

parts.prompt: Identify ONE detail in the image that shows protest against a tax.
parts.modelAnswer: One detail is the banner reading “NO TAX” carried in the crowd. Another is the banner reading “DOWN WITH TAX,” and the crowd also carries a tarred-and-feathered effigy on poles.

scoring.criterion: Names one detail showing protest against a tax, such as the “NO TAX” or “DOWN WITH TAX” banner or the effigy carried through the street.
scoring.notEarned: Describing the crowd without naming a detail tied to the tax does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Explain ONE way the image reflects the grievances of western Pennsylvania farmers.
parts.modelAnswer: The image shows a crowd carrying an effigy and banners against the tax, which reflects how fiercely the farmers opposed Hamilton’s excise on whiskey. Whiskey was how they turned grain into cash, so the tax struck at their livelihood and they answered with public protest and threats against tax collectors.

scoring.criterion: Explains one way the image reflects the farmers’ grievances, such as the anger at the whiskey excise, the use of public protest and effigies, or the threat to their livelihood.
scoring.notEarned: Saying only that the farmers were angry, without linking the image to their grievance, does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Explain ONE limit of the image as evidence about the Whiskey Rebellion.
parts.modelAnswer: The image is a 19th-century engraving made long after 1794, not a view drawn during the rebellion. It shows the protest as a dramatic street scene, but it cannot show what the farmers actually did or what Washington’s government actually faced, so it tells us more about how later Americans pictured the rebellion than about the events themselves.

scoring.criterion: Explains one limit of the image as evidence, such as that it is a later depiction rather than a view made in 1794, or that it shows a dramatic scene rather than what actually happened.
scoring.notEarned: Saying only that one image cannot show everything, with no specific limit, does not earn the point.
